solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fruit rot can be a little gross

blocks.note: a plum is a stone fruit
pish is a dismissive word for nonsense, as is rot

explanation.surface: Mouldy fruit can look a bit disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross' reads as disgusting, but here it means fat, so 'a little gross' is slightly overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can mean fat or bulky, and being only somewhat chubby is a mild version of that.

clue.text: Kiss and cuddle? That’ll get everyone in bed!

indicators.note: to get one thing in another is to put it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to pet is to kiss and fondle
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion that a bit of affection will get the whole household under the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' is a noun for a crude mattress, not the place everyone ends up; 'get ... in' together signal the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A pallet is a rough straw mattress or makeshift sleeping place on the floor.

clue.text: Drugs take an edge off of evening meals

indicators.note: removing an edge means trimming a letter from one end of the following word

blocks.note: suppers are evening meals

explanation.surface: A complaint that drug-taking spoils people's dinners.
explanation.walkthrough: The edge removed is the first letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppers is slang for stimulant drugs such as amphetamines, which lift the user's mood.

clue.text: Fancy outfit rep presented in a new way

indicators.note: showing something in a new way means rearranging it, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A sales representative shows off a stylish outfit in a fresh light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the outfit, but it is a noun: a small decorated cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a small iced cake, and a petit four is exactly such a dainty sweet served with coffee.

clue.text: Back girl describing Conservative as “inferior”

indicators.note: to describe can mean to draw a line around, so these words enclose another piece

blocks.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a lass is a girl
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A political article in which a supportive young woman calls a Tory second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: The enclosing piece is the two-word phrase 'back girl' read together, so the Conservative lands between its words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-class is of lower quality or status, hence lesser and not up to standard.

clue.text: Empty one container into another

indicators.note: putting something into another thing places it inside, so the first pieces sit within the last

blocks.note: another container: a vat is a large tank
a can is a container

explanation.surface: An instruction to pour the contents of one vessel into a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' looks like an instruction to pour, but it is the adjective, and the rest of the clue is a recipe rather than a request.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacant room or seat is unoccupied, with nothing or nobody in it.

clue.text: A man’s shadow?

blocks.note: taken as written
a gent is a man; the 's reads as 'is' joining to the definition

explanation.surface: A question about the dark outline a man casts.
explanation.walkthrough: A shadow is also someone who secretly follows a person, which spies do.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to tail them covertly, which is the work of a secret agent or detective.

clue.text: A nameless visionary with a distinctive nose?

indicators.note: lacking a name means losing N, the abbreviation for name

blocks.note: taken as written
a romantic is an idealistic dreamer

explanation.surface: An anonymous dreamer with a striking profile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nose' is not a face but a smell, as in wine-tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Nose is the scent of wine or food, and something strongly fragrant has a distinctive one.

clue.text: Tough youth grasping tattooist messed around

indicators.note: grasping means holding inside, so the first piece wraps round the second

blocks.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth-cult tough
a tattooist inks skin

explanation.surface: A young thug grabs a tattoo artist and causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker is to fiddle aimlessly with something, so having tinkered means having fiddled about.

clue.text: What could make those kissing turn red?

definitions.text: What could make those kissing turn red?

blocks.clueFragment: What could make those kissing turn red?
blocks.note: surface reading: something that makes kissing couples blush
setter's reading: the body parts that do the kissing, which a cosmetic colours red

explanation.walkthrough: 'Those kissing' sounds like people, so 'turn red' suggests embarrassment; it means the mouth itself being coloured.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip colour is a cosmetic applied to the mouth, often in shades of red.

clue.text: Horse leading woman away from her end

indicators.note: the end of the word goes away, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the heroine is the female lead

explanation.surface: A horse ahead of a woman rider who is far from the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for a hard drug, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is long-standing street slang for the opiate drug, alongside smack and H.

clue.text: Feel bad about sending off one right winger

indicators.note: sending something off removes it, so one letter is taken out

blocks.note: to regret is to feel bad about
R is right; one of the two Rs goes

explanation.surface: A football fan sorry that a right-sided wide player was sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests football, but here it is any creature with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are white herons, and any bird can jokingly be called something with wings.

clue.text: Horror of rider failing to start with horse in trial

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is missing

blocks.note: a knight is a mounted warrior
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A jousting knight's ordeal when his horse won't get going.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K of the rider is the letter that fails to start.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream is a horror, and any terrible ordeal is also called by this word.

clue.text: Awfully huge rodents one found in a tent?

definitions.text: Awfully huge rodents one found in a tent?

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the following letters are in a bad, jumbled order

blocks.note: the letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A camper's fright at finding enormous rats inside the tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the item spread on a tent floor is where a camper might find such creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundsheet is the waterproof sheet laid on the floor of a tent.

clue.text: Very happy nun in cooled pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are in a poor, scrambled state

blocks.note: the letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A nun delighted to be wearing chilled underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pants means underwear, and as slang it also means rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone in a state of blissful elation.

clue.text: Leadership speech full of empty rage

indicators.note: being full of something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other
an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: diction is manner of speaking
the first and last letters of rage

explanation.surface: A leader's address that is full of hollow anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Direction is guidance and management, the act of steering a group as its head.

clue.text: A lazy person might be really tired

blocks.note: first meaning: an idle loafer
second meaning: as two words, utterly exhausted

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a lazy person is merely tired; the answer is a noun for a loafer and also, split, a phrase for exhaustion.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout is called by this noun, and the split phrase means completely worn out.

clue.text: Hand over drugs?

blocks.note: first meaning: a poker hand of five cards in sequence
second meaning: no longer using them, clean

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a command to pass the drugs across; 'over' means finished with.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker a run of five consecutive cards has this name, and a former addict who is clean is said to be this.

clue.text: Turn and board coach with second to go

indicators.note: the second letter is to leave, so that position is removed

blocks.note: to board a vehicle is to enter it
a trainer coaches

explanation.surface: Instructions to swivel round and climb aboard a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' means a stage act, and 'coach' is a sports trainer, not a bus; the R of the trainer goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn is a variety-show act or performer, someone who amuses an audience.

clue.text: Don’t bother with warning shot

blocks.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout
a shot is an attempt, a go

explanation.surface: A golfer who can't be bothered to shout before a stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to do without it or pass it up; this spelling is a common variant.

clue.text: Go and have some food in a moment

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: a bit is a short while
to have food is to eat

explanation.surface: An invitation to pop off and grab a quick snack.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal order telling someone to leave at once, much like get lost.

clue.text: Ailing leader is dosing up, because of this?

definitions.text: Ailing leader is dosing up, because of this?

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept
things that are up are in disorder, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: the first letter of ailing
the letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A sick boss is taking medicine, prompted by what the doctor found.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the doctor's finding is why the sick boss is taking medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's identification of an illness is what leads to medicine being prescribed.

clue.text: Material helping to make many longboats

indicators.note: the letters help form the words that follow, sitting inside them

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A fabric used in building plenty of Viking vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric, used for clothing, ropes and sails.

clue.text: A quiet residential road in Settle

blocks.note: first meaning: a cul-de-sac of houses
second meaning: to conclude, as a deal

explanation.surface: A peaceful street in a small Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a market town in North Yorkshire, which makes it look like a place name rather than a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a dead-end street of houses has this name, and to conclude a sale or account is to do this.

clue.text: Nurses must protect limb that’s turned red

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the word is read backwards
protecting means surrounding, so the first piece wraps round the second

blocks.note: EN is an enrolled nurse, so ENS is nurses
a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: Nurses guard a limb that has gone red and inflamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' is a communist, not a colour; Engels co-wrote the Communist Manifesto.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels was a founding communist thinker, and a red is a communist.

clue.text: Householder with Hoover, perhaps, but no power

indicators.note: but no means without, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: Herbert Hoover was a US president; perhaps marks him as an example
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A homeowner with a vacuum cleaner but no electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoover suggests the vacuum cleaner, but it is the American president.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident lives in a particular dwelling, as an occupant of the home does.

clue.text: Powerful people settle back to ring Brown

indicators.note: going back means reading the preceding word from its end
ringing something encircles it, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: to settle is to sit down
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Influential figures return to telephone a man named Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Titans are figures of great strength or influence, after the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Do nut at working on ultimately useless project

indicators.note: working means being processed or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is taken

blocks.note: the letters used as fodder
the final letter of useless

explanation.surface: Someone toils on a doughnut as part of a hopeless venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' looks like a noun for a scheme, but it is the verb meaning to jut out.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to stick out or protrude, which is what the phrasal verb means physically.
